  1. Unauthenticated remote code execution in Nginx

    • Security

    1490 points · 639 comments · 18 Nov 2026, 15:19 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Wiz described two HTTP/2-related NGINX vulnerabilities, including an unauthenticated remote-code-execution issue under specific configurations. The report identified affected versions and listed patched NGINX OSS releases, while recommending upgrading or temporarily disabling HTTP/2 during remediation.

    Discussion — Discussion concentrated on exposure and disclosure timing: commenters debated whether public source commits or exploit-branded sites help attackers, and whether disabling HTTP/2 is practical for gRPC and related workloads. Technical replies distinguished the vulnerabilities’ conditions and urged patching.

  2. Java4Shell: RCE in OpenJDK when processing Base64

    • Security

    1178 points · 329 comments · 17 Nov 2026, 21:11 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Calif described Java4Shell, a remote-code-execution vulnerability affecting some OpenJDK Base64 processing paths. The report set out the affected conditions, proof-of-concept context, and remediation guidance.

    Discussion — The thread focused on exploitability, the affected parsing and deployment conditions, and how the issue compares with past Java vulnerabilities. Readers discussed patch urgency, dependency inventory, and whether the branding overstated the scope.

  3. Show HN: Nobody blocks a keyboard – Rooted Android as a physical USB Deck

    • Hardware
    • Security

    56 points · 57 comments · 16 Nov 2026, 14:18 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Emittr turns a rooted Android phone into a USB HID keyboard and mouse using the Linux USB gadget subsystem, intended for controlled or locked-down systems where host software cannot be installed. The author says it exposes a LAN web UI and does not store credentials on the rooted phone.

    Discussion — The thread concentrated on security and misuse: commenters compared it with BadUSB, questioned using it with air-gapped systems, and noted platforms and tools that block untrusted USB devices. Others suggested KVM-like extensions and alternatives.

  4. Show HN: Coral – Open-source gateway where agents write their own tools

    • AI
    • Security
    • Software Development

    52 points · 24 comments · 16 Nov 2026, 14:14 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Coral is an open-source, self-hosted gateway for agents that lets them write reusable TypeScript custom tools while enforcing policies and managed identities. The HN post says programs run in V8 isolates without direct network access or credentials.

    Discussion — Discussion examined code-mode agents, custom-tool reuse, policy boundaries, security, and claimed task speed and cost reductions. Readers asked how the system compares with MCP-style integrations and how it avoids unsafe permissions.

    • Email
    • Security

    123 points · 43 comments · 16 Nov 2026, 02:53 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — The Tell HN post warned that addresses published on HN, including in Who Is Hiring-style posts, were being used in phishing attempts, based on a unique email address that received a fake AWS-payment message.

    Discussion — Commenters compared aliases, catch-all addresses, spam filtering, and the trade-off between public contact information and abuse. The discussion shared phishing indicators and operational-security habits.
